title: These US Cities Spend the Most on Groceries
paragraphs: Food prices have been rising in many places, but the cost of groceries is a much bigger problem in some US cities than in others. A new study has looked at which cities spend the biggest share of their income on food.

The study was done by WalletHub, a personal finance website. It looked at 100 large US cities and compared the cost of 26 basic grocery items with the median household income in each city. The median is the middle point, so half of households earn more and half earn less. The data came from the US Census Bureau and the Council for Community and Economic Research.

According to the study, people in Detroit spend the largest share of their income on groceries. In Detroit, groceries take up about 4.03% of the median household income. Cleveland was second at 3.93%, and Birmingham, Alabama, was third at 3.45%.

At the other end of the list were some of the richest cities in California. In Fremont, groceries made up only 0.91% of median household income. San Jose and San Francisco followed, at 1.07% and 1.10%.

Interestingly, the cities where groceries are the biggest burden are not always the cities with the highest prices. In fact, Detroit's grocery prices are only the 36th most expensive on the list. Instead, the main reason for the difference is income. In Detroit, the median household income is less than $40,000 a year, and Cleveland has the lowest median household income of all the cities in the study.
According to WalletHub, this shows that the cost of food depends more on how much people earn than on the prices in stores.
A separate study by the website Cheapism looked only at grocery prices. It found that Honolulu, Hawaii, has the most expensive groceries, with prices about 31% higher than the national average.
